reason: The text portrays the Hebrews (Israelites) as Yahweh's people through several key elements: (1) The repeated phrase 'בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל' (children of Israel) designates them as a distinct people under Yahweh's care; (2) The divine statement 'שַׁלַּח עַמִּי וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי' ('Let my people go and they shall serve me') explicitly frames the Hebrews as Yahweh's followers and servants; (3) The narrative demonstrates Yahweh's special protection of the Israelites in Goshen, shielding them from the plagues that afflict Egypt; (4) Moses acts as Yahweh's representative, communicating divine will to Pharaoh on behalf of the Hebrew people; (5) The text establishes Yahweh as 'אֱלֹהֵינוּ' (our God), indicating a covenantal relationship. The entire passage is structured to show the Hebrews as God's chosen people, distinguished from other nations through divine protection and intended service.
